name: Zercher Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A Bulgarian split squat variation where the barbell is cradled in the crooks of the elbows rather than placed across the upper back. The Zercher position forces a more upright torso, increases core bracing demands significantly, and shifts loading stress away from the spine while still providing strong quadriceps and glute stimulus.

execution.starting_position: Stand in a split stance with the rear foot elevated on a bench. Cradle the barbell in the crooks of both elbows, holding your forearms parallel to the floor.
execution.setup_instructions: Set a barbell to roughly waist height in a rack. Cradle it in your elbow crooks, secure the grip, then walk to the bench and position your rear foot on it.
steps: Step 1: Brace your core hard and keep your torso upright throughout the movement.
Step 2: Lower your rear knee toward the floor by bending both knees, maintaining an upright torso.
Step 3: Descend until the front thigh is at or below parallel to the floor.
Step 4: Drive through the front heel to return to the starting position, fully extending the front hip and knee.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before descending. Exhale at the top after completing the rep.
common_mistakes: Letting the torso collapse forward under the Zercher load
Allowing the front knee to cave inward during the ascent
safety_considerations: The Zercher position can stress the forearms and biceps tendons — use padding if needed and avoid very heavy loads initially
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower until the front thigh is parallel to the floor or below. Keep the rear shin roughly vertical.
coaching_cues: Drive the floor away with your front heel
